rule_context:
COMPLIANCE NOTE - Advertising Substantiation (Health Claims)

Any advertising claim that a product is "clinically proven" or otherwise asserts a proven health benefit requires competent and reliable scientific evidence on file before the copy is used in any campaign. Competent and reliable evidence means human clinical data demonstrating the specific health outcome claimed, conducted and reported in a manner consistent with recognized standards in the relevant field. In vitro studies, animal models, formulation or strain-survival data, and general ingredient research do not substantiate a clinical claim of proven efficacy in humans. A claim that a product is "clinically studied" is only permissible when the referenced study meets the competent and reliable evidence standard for the health outcome described. Claims limited to laboratory or formulation attributes (e.g., lab-tested, survives stomach acid) do not require clinical evidence but must accurately describe the testing performed and must not imply health outcomes beyond what was measured. If no human clinical evidence on file supports the specific health benefit claimed, the claim "clinically proven" is out of scope and may not appear in copy regardless of projected performance. Substantiation files must be reviewed and approved by Legal before any clinical claim ships. When in doubt, use the narrowest accurate description of the evidence available.
